Beat 'lowest' ('Its lowest point sits 115 m below the waves', fact1 = 115 m, the depth reveal): not confirmed, sources disagree. The Geological Society geosite (geolsoc.org.uk/GeositesChannelTunnel, fetched) says 'lowest point at 115 m below sea surface level ... rock cover at its greatest, 75m' but the same page also says 'At its lowest point, it is 75 m (250 ft) deep'. The operator Eurotunnel/LeShuttle (leshuttle.com interesting-facts page, fetched) says 'The Channel Tunnel is 75 metres below sea level at its deepest point', and Wikipedia's Channel Tunnel article (fetched) says '75 m (246 ft) below sea level'. Only Discovery UK (discoveryuk.com) clearly backs 115 m below sea level / 75 m below seabed. The operator is the most official source (profile: the most official wins), so 115 m below the waves can't be stated as fact. This is the topic's own verify item 1, still open.

Fix: rewrite the 'lowest' beat and fact1 to a figure the sources agree on, e.g. the tunnels run on average about 45 m below the seabed (Wikipedia 'on average, 45 m (148 ft) below the seabed'; geolsoc 'UK seaward drive ... about 45m below sea bed'), or say the lowest point without a number. Note that 75 m is also contested (below sea level per Eurotunnel and Wikipedia, rock cover per geolsoc), so 75 m is no safe swap unless worded so both readings hold.

Checked and fine: fact2 37.9 km undersea (Wikipedia page shows '37.9 km (23.5 miles)'; Discovery UK gives 37.9 km; Eurotunnel gives 38 km, the same figure rounded); chalk marl tunnelling, two rail tunnels plus a central service tunnel for maintenance and rescue, undersea crossover caverns, the London-Paris trains; meter prints no unsourced depths (ft is placement only); description ends with the channel disclaimer; no advice or tone issues.

Beat 'deep' ('On average, it runs 45 m below the seabed', fact1 = 45 m, Wikipedia): the operator contradicts it. Getlink, the tunnel's owner and operator (getlinkgroup.com/uk/the-channel-tunnel, fetched), says the three tunnels were 'bored at an average 40m below the sea bed', and its LeShuttle facts page (fetched) says 'runs an average of 40 metres below the sea bed'. The builder Vinci's page also says 40 m. The 45 m comes from Wikipedia and ICE (ice.org.uk returned 403; a search snippet reads 'On average, the tunnels are 45m below the sea bed'). The profile says the most official source wins, and that is the operator, so 45 m isn't confirmed. Fix: set fact1 to 40 m with source Getlink and url https://www.getlinkgroup.com/uk/the-channel-tunnel/, change the world note to 'Depths: Getlink · not to scale', and add Getlink to the description's Sources line. The beat's wording can stay.

Checked and fine: fact2 37.9 km under the sea (the Wikipedia page shows it; Discovery UK gives 37.9 km; the operator gives the same length rounded, 37 km on Getlink and 38 km on LeShuttle; I accept it with this note); the cavern line (Getlink: two crossovers under the sea, 7 km off the English coast and 13 km off the French coast); the service tunnel between the two rail tunnels (Getlink); tunnelling in chalk; the 115 m claim is gone; the meter prints no unsourced depths; the description ends with the channel disclaimer; no advice or tone issues.
